source_note: Derived from HS-T005 Turns 4-6 and refined by HS-T008 / thread 3100b354. Audit note: HS-T005 Turn 6 headlines '18 Languages across 9 Major Families' and '17 Founding Canonical Texts', but its itemized breakdown sums to 16 named languages (6+2+2+1+1+1+1+1+1) and 16 text bullets (grouping Analects/Dao De Jing/I Ching together). Those 16 attested Turn-6 entries carry status 'turn6-core'; the two Turn-4/5/roadmap additions (Avestan/Old Persian and Korean, or Ge'ez) carry status 'archive-expansion' so both counts are transparent.

pathways.label: Vedic Sanskrit
pathways.notes: Archaic Indo-European morphology and pitch accent; historically oral before Brahmic/Devanagari manuscript transmission.

pathways.label: Classical Sanskrit
pathways.notes: Explicit phonological-morphological derivation rules foundational to modern linguistics.

pathways.label: Homeric / Epic Greek
pathways.notes: Mixed Ionic-Aeolic Kunstsprache; primary mythic-literary anchor.

pathways.label: Hellenistic Koine Greek
pathways.notes: Distinct syntactic and lexical register from Homer; essential for Hebrew-to-Greek translation chains (e.g., dabar -> logos, shalom -> eirene).

pathways.label: Classical / Augustan Latin
pathways.notes: Primary poetic and mythic transformation lineage leading toward Dante.

pathways.label: Late / Ecclesiastical Latin
pathways.notes: Transmission bridge rendering Hebrew and Koine Greek biblical terminology into Western European vernaculars.

pathways.label: Old East Slavic to Modern Russian
founding_texts: Slovo o polku Igoreve (Tale of Igor's Campaign, late 12th c.)
pathways.notes: Demonstrates Balto-Slavic sound changes and Cyrillic orthographic adaptation.

pathways.label: Insular West Saxon Poetic Koine
pathways.notes: Uses Insular Latin script augmented with thorn (þ), eth (ð), ash (æ), and wynn (ƿ).

pathways.label: Late 14th-c. London Middle English
pathways.notes: Included for historical-evolutionary continuity (Old -> Middle -> Modern English). Active phonological transcription, final -e scansion, and corpus tooling live in 4444J99/chaucer.

pathways.label: Biblical Hebrew (Masoretic vocalization)
pathways.notes: Trilateral consonantal root morphology (binyanim); portions of Daniel and Ezra are in Biblical Aramaic.

pathways.label: Quranic / Classical Arabic (Fusha)
pathways.notes: Highly regular trilateral/quadrilateral root-and-pattern morphology (awzan) and cursive rasm + i'jam orthography.

pathways.label: Pre-Qin Classical Chinese
pathways.notes: Source system for East Asian morphosyllabic characters; concise analytic syntax with high polysemy.

languages.name: Classical & Modern Japanese
languages.branch: Japonic (grouped under East Asian/Sinospheric in HS-T005; genetically Japonic, distinct from Sino-Tibetan)

pathways.label: Early & Classical Japanese
pathways.notes: Audit note: HS-T005 grouped Japanese with Classical Chinese by script borrowing; linguistically Japanese belongs to the Japonic family and combines morphographic kanji with moraic kana.

pathways.label: Old / Sangam Tamil
pathways.notes: Non-Indo-European agglutinative classical tradition of South India; native Tamil Brahmic abugida planned for dedicated glyph expansion.

pathways.label: Classical Malay (Jawi Arabic script & Rumi Latin script)
pathways.notes: Illustrates Austronesian affixation/reduplication and cross-family script adaptation (Arabic -> Jawi -> Latin).

pathways.label: Kalevalaic / Standard Finnish
pathways.notes: Non-Indo-European European language featuring rich agglutinative case morphology and vowel harmony.

pathways.label: Classical Swahili (Ajami Arabic & Latin orthography)
founding_texts: Utenzi wa Tambuka (1728) and classical Utenzi verse
pathways.notes: Bantu noun-class concord system combined with Indian Ocean Arabic lexical contact.

pathways.label: Old Anatolian / Ottoman to 1928 Modern Latin Reform
pathways.notes: Agglutinative suffixation and vowel harmony; primary historical case study in deliberate national script transition (1928).

pathways.label: 16th-c. Classical Nahuatl
founding_texts: Florentine Codex (Historia general de las cosas de Nueva Espana)
pathways.notes: Polysynthetic morphology and noun incorporation recorded in adapted Latin orthography alongside Indigenous pictorial traditions.

pathways.label: 15th-c. Hunminjeongeum & Modern Korean
founding_texts: Yongbieocheonga (Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven)
pathways.notes: Featured in HS-T005 Turn 5, HS-T009, and HS-F013 for featural script design.

pathways.label: Classical Ge'ez
pathways.notes: Featured in HS-T005 Turn 4 and HS-F013 (#10) as the South Semitic abugida ('fidel') exemplar.
